summary: Missouri Conservation Commission tower in Taney County, built 1951-52; a 1953 survey describes a steel structure about 120 feet tall; its survey station is marked removed.

facts.design: Four-legged steel structure supporting an observation cabin (1953 survey)
facts.status_note: Survey station marked removed on the site. No source describes what remains at the site today.

events.note: Towersite acquired and tower erected, fiscal 1951-52 (annual report quoted on the site)
Coast and Geodetic Survey station described about 2 miles south-southeast of Cedar Creek; overall height about 120 ft to the roof apex

evidence.supports: Missouri Conservation Commission tower, Taney County, location 22N-18W-30
evidence.quote: Missouri Lookouts - Taney County - Missouri Conservation Commission - 22N-18W-30

evidence.supports: Towersite acquired and tower erected, FY 1951-52
evidence.quote: A towersite was acquired and a tower erected

evidence.supports: 1953 survey: four-legged steel structure with observation cabin, about 120 ft

evidence.supports: Survey height point is the apex of the roof

evidence.supports: Station about 2 miles SSE of Cedar Creek, 1 mile east of County Highway K
evidence.quote: THE STATION IS ABOUT 2 MILES SOUTH-SOUTHEAST OF CEDAR CREEK AND 1 MILE EAST OF COUNTY HIGHWAY K.

notes_for_editor: One source: the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes a Missouri Conservation Commission annual report (FY 1951-52) and a 1953 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description. The originals were not reached. The 120 ft figure runs to the roof apex, not the cab floor, so no height_m. No removal date is given. The 'Removed' label sits above the NGS survey-station block, so the story attributes removal to the survey station, not the tower. A Hercules Glades fire tower (Taney County, 1936, from a travel listing) appeared in searches; it is a different site and was not used.
